ella_ml: quick heads-up — ran a focused sensitivity sweep for weight-only int8 (bitsandbytes / llm.int8) on voyager-13b-cpu-backend (actually GPU: a100-80g), want to capture surprising deltas before we consider a canary

ella_ml: sweep axes: group_size=[32,64,128], skip_layers=[0,2,4], batch=[1,4,16], temp=[0.0,0.7,1.0], enable_kv_cache=[on,off] — used our standard summarization slice (1000 prompts)

sam_devx: nice. did you compare against fp16 baseline or gptq baseline?

ella_ml: fp16 baseline only for this pass. gptq followup planned if we see promising cost wins. fp16 latency: p50=210ms p95=420ms for batch=1

lucy_research: any quality metrics? rouge/bertscore?

ella_ml: pasted quick summary below (relative to fp16):
```
group=32 skip=0 batch=1 kv=on temp=0.0 -> rougeL -0.8 pts, bertscore -0.006, p95 +15ms
group=64 skip=0 batch=1 kv=on temp=0.0 -> rougeL -1.6 pts, bertscore -0.012, p95 +10ms
group=128 skip=0 batch=1 kv=on temp=0.0 -> rougeL -2.9 pts, bertscore -0.020, p95 -5ms
group=64 skip=2 batch=4 kv=on temp=0.7 -> rougeL -1.1 pts, bertscore -0.009, p95 -20ms
group=32 skip=4 batch=16 kv=off temp=1.0 -> rougeL -3.8 pts, bertscore -0.035, p95 -60ms
```

ella_ml: interestingly higher group_size reduced latency but hurt quality non-linearly. temp makes it worse for long-form prompts (temp=1.0 amplifies hallucination errors)

sam_devx: so best tradeoff looks like group=32/64 with skip_layers=2? that middle ground gives small quality hit for decent perf improvement?

ella_ml: yeah, skip=2 (skip first two transformer blocks for quant) seems to recover ~0.5 rougeL vs skip=0 at same group=64. hypothesis: early layers are sensitive — consistent with prior papers

archie_sre: what about memory / capacity? we need numbers for dedicated pools (reserved) to update deployment profiles

ella_ml: memory footprint: int8 w-only reduced GPU memory delta ~ -25% vs fp16 for group<=64, ~-33% at group=128. kv_cache on increases working set by ~6% (expected).

lucy_research: did you check prompt-length stratification? short vs long?

ella_ml: yes — short prompts (<=64 tokens) saw almost no quality delta; long prompts (>512) degraded most (rouge drop 2-4 pts depending on group). suggests we should gate int8 w-only behind prompt-length routing or cache-aware routing

sam_devx: can we do a quick canary config suggestion?

ella_ml: suggested canary: route 10% traffic -> int8 w-only with config: group=64 skip=2 kv=on batch=1 temp clamp at 0.9 for sampler endpoints; monitoring hooks: rougeL slice, token-level hallucination rate, p95 latency, rejection rate. rollback if rougeL delta >1.5 on canary slice

archie_sre: add cost delta estimate pls

ella_ml: rough cost model: tokens/sec improves ~1.3x at group=64 -> ~23% lower infra cost for steady-state; but quality regression risk concentrated in longform slices

ops-bot: deployment check: no active incidents. recommended to schedule canary outside peak window 02:00-06:00 UTC :calendar:

sam_devx: will create canary config PR with TTL and auto-rollback flags. thanks el! :thumbsup:

lucy_research: can I get the full csv of per-prompt diffs? I want to craft targeted eval slices (legal/finance/longform).

ella_ml: uploading now to /mnt/evals/int8_sweeps/voyager13b/2067504321_sweep.csv — flagged columns: prompt_len, rougeL_delta, bertscore_delta, group, skip, batch, kv

sam_devx: perfect. let's keep this thread as the reference for rollout notes. follow-ups: gptq compare + regen with mixed-quant (awq) next week.

ella_ml: noted. i'll schedule gptq/awq runs and ping when csvs ready.
